_comment: The stamped LINKED tier: how many matched translation units actually reach the
PC port's binary. This is a STAMP, not a live counter, and it cannot be anything
else from main: port/tools/linkage.py reads build/port/walk_window.map, which only
exists after an MSVC build of the port, and CI on main has no such build.
BEFORE STAMPING, LOOK FOR A BUILD THAT ALREADY EXISTS. Every port lane carries its
own build tree, so a current walk_window.map is usually already on disk:
ls -la */build/port/walk_window.map
across the port worktrees, newest first, then run the tool against that root. The
first version of this file was stamped off a five-day-old branch while a map from
the night before sat unread one directory away, and published 26.5% when the real
figure was 34.5%. A stale stamp is still a real measurement, just of the wrong run.
To refresh: run `python port/tools/linkage.py [root]` and update the numbers below
together with branch, commit and measuredAt. Never move the count without also
moving the provenance fields - tools/tiers.py drops a stamp missing any of them,
which is the intended behaviour for a number nobody can trace.
basis records what the figure is a measurement OF. The port branches are not merged,
so this is the best single lane rather than a combined total. All seven live lanes,
lk5 3819. Overlapping but not identical seats, so the merged figure is higher and
the published number stays a floor.
This number moves ONE way: seating a new actor class, worth ~8-10 TUs each.
Enrolling free TUs does nothing, because the release build dead-strips whatever the
linked closure never references.
basis: integration branch port/link100 at its pushed tip d19ed9da6, measured against that tip's own battery build walk_window.map (C:/tmp/l4seat, tree clean, battery ALL GREEN at floor 10032, five proofs green including the opening-cutscene gate). +20 over the 2026-09-07 stamp of 10013 on a4504f88d and +912 over the 2026-08-30 stamp of 9121 on cons ce1afba51. The shipping branch port-mount-noseat-cluster is fast-forwarded to the same commit. Since the 10013 stamp: every linker alias whose two sides name different things was checked against the ROM (2391 directives, 461 adjudicated by RTTI name string or referrer set, 3 wrong, 42 justifications written, no number change); the 414-row documented host-ABI exception queue was censused by mechanism (209 rows are not port work; the 153-row pointer-to-member family is being measured row by row for one later batch); MgSnowball came off a generated virtual-call row; the TextureSequence deleting slot got its cdecl thunk instead of a live null; seventeen slot-5 render bodies came back onto their matched TUs once the Model-family vtable numbering they cited stopped existing; and the cutscene models' two complete-object destructors got real faces, one of which had never been linked. Gated rungs since the last stamp: 10013 -> 10032 -> 10033. The run's earlier content (the ROM's save system, thread scheduler and ARM9<->ARM7 link as ROM code; the pre-main boot spans; Stage vtable slots 3/6/9/16/17; the boot and download-play scenes; /vmg /vmm target-wide; the Model-family virtual-destructor unfold; 24 ruled bodies seated by ROM address; CAGE_LIFT, RICKSHAW_BDW and PUSHABLE_BLOCK registered; TRAP moved off LIGHT_BEAM's vtable) is described in the 10013 stamp's history. The linkage number is cartridge-independent (an identical TU set links with no ROM present, locally and on a GitHub runner). Remaining: the documented host-ABI exception queue, the wireless chain behind the ARM7 model (~175), the boot chain's refused arms, and guessed vtable bodies that need real decomp.
